title: The Chase
paragraphs: An NBC dramatic anthology in which every story is built around a pursuit or race against danger, moving freely among crime, adventure, suspense, and occasional science fiction.

NBC dramatic anthology built around hunter/hunted situations across crime, adventure, suspense, fantasy, horror and occasional science fiction. The GRH snapshot contains 51 broadcasts from episodes 4-55; episodes 1-3 and 30 are absent from this frozen subset.
GRH documents the program through NBC sustaining run (April 27, 1952 to June 28, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Lawrence Klee (writer on 48 recordings, creator on 47 recordings, and director on 1 recording), Fred Collins (announcer on 43 recordings), Fred Weihe (director on 27 recordings and transcriber on 27 recordings), Edward King (director on 9 recordings and transcriber on 6 recordings), Leon Janney (performer on 9 recordings), Roger De Koven (performer on 9 recordings), and Daniel Sutter (director on 8 recordings and transcriber on 8 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include pursuit, escape and hunter/hunted situations, murder and homicide, fraud, blackmail and financial schemes, espionage, Cold War and international intrigue, science fiction and speculative threats, and ghosts and supernatural threats.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including NBC sustaining anthology production, Cold War-era pursuit stories, and Cross-genre anthology experimentation.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (73 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (49 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (40 shared credited people), [[show|dimension-x|Dimension X]] (44 shared credited people), and [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (37 shared credited people).
